id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

baseModel.description:
{@link ReliabilityMlModel} over which this scenario is based.

During the scenario execution, we will use the {@link MlPipeline} of this model to
generate predictions.

timeRange.description: The time range over which the scenario is executed.

displayStatus.description: The translated status of the scenario, which is used for display purposes.

translatedStatusKey.description: The translation key for the status of the scenario, which is used for display purposes.

scenarioPipelineData.description:
Scenario {@link ReliabilityMlModel#xFeatures} data, which is used to generate #alertData, #algorithmData, and
#featureOutputData using the {@link MlPipeline} of #baseModel.

**NOTE**: {@link Map} is defined as `<string, any>` instead of `<string, Data>` because the metadata system is
          not persisting the map correctly, so we can use `any` to store it as a `Boxed<json>` instead.

alertData.description:
{@link Data} output from the {@link ReliabilityMlModel#process} and {@link ReliabilityMlModel#interpret} steps over #baseModel.

This DataFrame stores the timestamps when alerts were generated and contains columns for each model feature
used to generate them (feature contributions).

```
| timestamp           | feature1 | feature2 | featureN |
|---------------------|----------|----------|----------|
| 2024-01-01 00:00:00 | 0.5      | 0.2      | 0.3      |  // All values are normalized
| 2024-01-16 00:00:00 | 0.6      | 0.2      | 0.2      |
```

The process to generate this DataFrame is as follows:
- Run {@link ReliabilityMlModel#process} on the #baseModel and extract the primary model output for alerts
  ({@link ReliabilityMl.Project#alertOutputs}).
- Run {@link ReliabilityMlModel#interpret} on the #baseModel and extract the feature contribution data
  (`featureInterpretations`).

algorithmData.description:
{@link Data} output from the {@link ReliabilityMlModel#process} over the #baseModel

This DataFrame contains a column per {@link ReliabilityMl.Project#algorithmOutputs}, stored as a timeseries.

```
| timestamp           | riskScore | riskScoreNormalized |
|---------------------|-----------|---------------------|
| 2024-01-01 00:00:00 | 100       | 0.66                |
| 2024-01-02 00:00:00 | 150       | 1.0                 |
| 2024-01-03 00:00:00 | 120       | 0.80                |
| 2024-01-04 00:00:00 | 130       | 0.86                |
```

originalAlgorithmData.description:
{@link Data} output from the {@link ReliabilityMlModel#process} over the #baseModel but using persisted
{@link Feature}s data instead of #scenarioPipelineData, and is stored the same as #algorithmData.

featureOutputData.description:
A map of {@link Feature#id}s to the {@link Data} output from the {@link ReliabilityMlModel#process} and indexed
through {@link ReliabilityMl.Project#featureOutputs}.

**NOTE**: {@link Map} is defined as `<string, any>` instead of `<string, Data>` because the metadata system is
          not persisting the map correctly, so we can use `any` to store it as a `Boxed<json>` instead.

spec.description: The spec used to generate the scenario.

uiData.description: File containing the serialized UI data for the scenario.

workflowRun.description:
Automatically set by the orchestrator when the Workflow finishes.
It contains the {@link Workflow.Run} that was executed for this scenario.
This is used to track the execution of the scenario and to retrieve the errors if any.

title:
Entity representing a scenario for a {@link ReliabilityMlModel}, where we will use "fake" or "custom"
data to generate predictions using the model's {@link MlPipeline}.
name: ReliabilityMlModelScenario
